methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
REGENT Craft is a Series A transportation company founded by Billy Thalheimer and Mike Klinker that has raised $60M to date. The Transportation sector comprises 8 private peers (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero) and no public comparables. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage precedents meeting valuation-tier thresholds within Transportation.

The stage-progression method anchors the analysis. Using total capital raised of $60M as a baseline proxy for implied post-money valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields $120M. This represents a straightforward application of observed step-up patterns between funding rounds and does not depend on peer multiples or sector-specific metrics.

The triangulated range derived from this single applicable method is $102M (low), $120M (median), to $138M (high). The range reflects inherent uncertainty around exact timing of the next funding event and round structure rather than methodological disagreement. Key risks to valuation include the nascent state of the Transportation venture landscape (limiting peer density) and reliance on a single method with modest empirical depth. A peer-median cross-check would strengthen conviction if additional same-stage Transportation comparables become available. The $120M median represents the most defensible point estimate given current data constraints.
